newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mulls shift away from U.S. soybean supplies.
newsitem.headline: Manila mulls shift away from U.S. soybean supplies.

text.p: Philippine soymeal and soybean buyers are mulling a shift from the United States, where the country buys most of its requirements, to other suppliers as U.S. supplies are currently tight, traders said on Wednesday.

The prospect was raised even though U.S. soybean futures fell overnight after the release of a bearishly-construed report from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) which kept its soybean ending stocks estimate unchanged at 140 million bushels.

"The USDA soybean crop figures were slightly better than our expectations. However, we expect Philippine buyers to tap other sources like South American suppliers in their search for better prices," a trader for a Manila-based commodity house said.

Philippine soybean and soymeal buyers are expected to flock to South America, which is expected to harvest a bumper soybean crop this year, one trader said. The country's soymeal imports in 1997 are likely to rise to 1.4 million tonnes from last year's 1.2 million tonnes. Philippine firms buy an average of 20,000 tonnes of soybeans a month, traders said.
Soymeal is used mainly as animal feed in the Philippines' livestock and poultry industry.
In 1996, the Philippines bought about 55 percent of its soybeans and soymeal from the United States and 30 percent from Brazil. The remainder came from India, Argentina and China.
